lessons.title: What is CSS?
lessons.description: How CSS styles HTML, the syntax of a CSS rule, and the three ways to add CSS to a page.
hints: A CSS rule is written as selector { property: value; }, e.g. h1 { color: navy; }
Every declaration ends with a semicolon. A missing semicolon merges two declarations into one invalid one, so both stop working.
CSS comments start with /* and end with */. Writing // does not create a comment in CSS and silently breaks the next rule.
In this platform, the CSS tab is your external stylesheet. It is linked to the page by the <link> element in the HTML <head>.

lessons.title: Selectors
lessons.description: Targeting elements by type, class and ID, and styling several elements with one rule.
hints: Class selectors start with a full stop (.card) and ID selectors start with a hash (#contact). Neither symbol is used in the HTML attribute itself.
Class and ID names are case-sensitive, so the name in your CSS must match the HTML exactly.
To style several selectors with one rule, separate them with commas: h1, h2, h3 { ... }
If a style does not appear, check the selector's spelling first. This is the most common cause.

lessons.title: Colours and Backgrounds
lessons.description: Setting text and background colours in different formats, and adding background images.
hints: color sets the text colour; background-color sets the colour behind the content.
Hex colours start with # and have either 3 or 6 characters, e.g. #333 or #94248C.
The last value in rgba() and hsla() is the transparency, from 0 (fully transparent) to 1 (fully solid).
opacity makes an element and everything inside it transparent. To make only the background transparent, use a background colour with alpha instead.
Background images use url(), e.g. background-image: url('images/coast.jpg'); Check the path and file name if the image does not appear.

lessons.title: Units and Typography
lessons.description: Sizing with CSS units, choosing and loading fonts, and styling text.
hints: rem is relative to the root (html) font size; em is relative to the font size of the element's parent.
Font names containing spaces need quotes, e.g. font-family: "Open Sans", Arial, sans-serif;
Always end a font stack with a generic family such as sans-serif or serif, in case none of the other fonts are available.
A Google Fonts <link> goes in the HTML <head>. The font-family declaration that uses it goes in your CSS.
line-height works best without a unit, e.g. line-height: 1.5; which means 1.5 times the font size.

lessons.title: The Cascade, Inheritance and Specificity
lessons.description: How the browser decides which rule wins when several rules style the same element.
hints: When two rules have the same specificity, the one that comes later in the CSS wins.
An ID selector beats any number of class selectors, and a class selector beats any number of element selectors.
Text properties such as color and font-family are inherited by child elements. Box properties such as border and padding are not.
Avoid !important. If a rule is not applying, make its selector more specific or move it later instead.

lessons.title: Display and the Box Model
lessons.description: How every element is a box, and how display, padding, borders and margins control its size and spacing.
hints: width, height and vertical margins have no effect on inline elements such as <span> and <a>. Use display: inline-block; or display: block; first.
With box-sizing: border-box; the width includes the padding and border, which makes sizes much easier to predict.
Shorthand values go clockwise from the top: margin: top right bottom left; e.g. margin: 10px 20px 10px 20px;
margin: 0 auto; only centres a block element if it has a width smaller than its container.

lessons.title: Positioning
lessons.description: Moving elements out of the normal flow with relative, absolute, fixed and sticky positioning, and layering them with z-index.
hints: top, right, bottom and left only work when position is set to something other than static.
An absolutely positioned element is placed relative to its nearest positioned ancestor. Add position: relative; to the parent to control where it goes.
z-index only works on positioned elements (and on flex and grid items). A higher value sits in front of a lower one.
position: sticky; needs a position value such as top: 0; to know where to stick.

lessons.title: Combinators and Pseudo-Selectors
lessons.description: Selecting elements by their relationships and states, and styling parts of elements with pseudo-elements.
hints: A space selects descendants at any depth (nav a); > selects direct children only (ul > li).
Style link states in this order, or some will not appear: :link, :visited, :hover, :focus, :active.
::before and ::after need a content property to appear, even if it is empty: content: "";
:nth-child() accepts odd, even or a formula, e.g. li:nth-child(odd) or li:nth-child(3n).

lessons.title: Layout: Flexbox and Grid
lessons.description: Arranging content in rows, columns and grids with flexbox and CSS grid, and choosing between them.
hints: display: flex; and display: grid; go on the parent (the container), not on the items inside it.
In flexbox, justify-content aligns items along the main axis and align-items aligns them along the cross axis.
flex-direction: column; swaps the axes, so justify-content then works vertically.
grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); creates three equal columns. fr means a fraction of the available space.
gap adds space between items in both flex and grid layouts, without adding space around the outside.

lessons.title: Styling Lists, Tables and Forms
lessons.description: Applying everything so far to build navigation menus, readable tables and accessible forms.
hints: To remove bullets from a list, use list-style: none; together with padding: 0; to remove the indent as well.
border-collapse: collapse; on the table merges the double borders between cells into single lines.
For striped rows, select every other row with tr:nth-child(even).
Form controls do not inherit fonts by default. Add font: inherit; to inputs, selects and buttons.
Never remove the outline on :focus without adding another clear focus style. Keyboard users need it to see where they are.

lessons.title: Responsive Design
lessons.description: Making pages adapt to any screen size with the viewport tag, flexible images and media queries.
hints: The viewport <meta> tag goes in the HTML <head>. Without it, phones display the page zoomed out as if on a desktop screen.
img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; } stops images overflowing their container on small screens.
In mobile-first CSS, write styles for small screens first, then use @media (min-width: ...) to add changes for larger screens.
Media queries respond to the width of the preview. Open the pop-out preview and drag its edge to test each breakpoint.

lessons.title: Consolidation: Style and Validate
lessons.description: Style the Beginners' Web Workshop page from a brief and check your CSS with the W3C validator.
hints: Style the page in stages: base text and colours first, then the box model, then layout, then responsive changes.
Validate by copying all of your CSS into the "By direct input" tab of the W3C CSS Validation Service.
Fix validator errors from the top down. A missing brace can cause errors in every rule after it.
Check your text and background colours have enough contrast to be easy to read.
